sections.heading: EL Go/No-Go for Glamsterdam (EIP-8037 as-is)
sections.summary: All EL client teams gave green light to ship Glamsterdam with EIP-8037 unchanged; no team vetoed.
sections.body:
- Ansgar marshalled an EL-side decision carried over from the previous ACDE call: commit to Glamsterdam as-is or delay into 2027 for spec changes to EIP-8037.
- **Geth** (Felix): no strong alternative proposal exists; leaning toward shipping as-is rather than re-architecting, which would delay the fork significantly.
- **Reth** (Dragan): supports EIP-8037 as-is; wants to ship Glamsterdam as soon as possible; a delay of a few months would be too long.
- **ethrex** (Iván): supports moving forward with the current spec, assuming affected parties are contacted and helped to upgrade in time.
- **Nethermind** (Łukasz): had very slight preference for Toni's proposed spec variants (5.2 or 5.3) but acknowledged they are not clearly worth doing at this stage; will not block shipping.
  - Ben Adams confirmed Nethermind would not veto.
- **Besu** (Luis Pinto): posted a late proposal to defer state gas refills to end-of-transaction, but acknowledged it has edge cases (griefing via gas, GAS opcode monotonicity issues) and is not strong enough; abstained rather than block.
  - Expressed concern that the GAS opcode is becoming unusable post-Glamsterdam due to non-monotonic gas behaviour.
- **Erigon** (Andrew / Paweł): acknowledged 8037 breaks some invariants but called it the lesser evil; uncertain but not blocking.
- Toni Wahrstätter summarised in chat: no spec-change alternative is clearly better; full deferral of refills opens larger griefing attacks (e.g. EIP-4337, calls to untrusted contracts); patterns app devs need should be addressed natively post-Glamsterdam.
- Ansgar noted no client unambiguously favoured delay, while several were unambiguously in favour of proceeding.
- Decision: EL green light to proceed with Glamsterdam on current spec.
- Ethlabs also published a [position statement](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/ethlabs-position-on-glamsterdam/30518) supporting shipping Glamsterdam as-is.

sections.heading: CL Builder-Payload Validation Fix (PR 5770 vs PR 5820)
sections.summary: Consensus layer adopted PR 5770 (RLP-based, non-consensus-breaking) for Glamsterdam; PR 5820 deferred to a future fork.
sections.body:
- Issue: the CL does not currently verify the execution payload block hash, allowing a malicious builder to sign multiple bids with different payloads, which can cause problems for payload timeliness votes.
- [PR 5770](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5770): imports RLP into the CL to recompute and verify the block hash during gossip validation. Non-consensus-breaking but introduces RLP dependency into the CL.
- [PR 5820](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5820): commits to the hash-tree-root of the payload in the bid. Cleaner (no RLP), but consensus-breaking; would also break Sepolia and a running devnet.
- Ben Edgington expressed strong preference for the non-breaking fix, arguing delay at this stage requires a security-critical justification.
- **Teku** (Enrico): weak support for 5770; noted 5820 with signatures removed would add hidden complexity (changed verification flows, pool protections). A middle ground (5820 keeping signatures) exists but is still consensus-breaking.
- **Nimbus** (Dustin): prefers 5820; raised concern that RLP may never fully go away, because backfilling blocks from this period would still need it.
  - Acknowledged the ~5-month backfill window means the dependency eventually expires in practice.
  - Ultimately would not block 5770, calling it sufficiently pragmatic.
- **Grandine** (Saulius): prefers 5820 but willing to accept 5770 if there is general consensus to ship faster.
- **Lodestar** (Nico): prefers 5820 but agrees it is not warranted to delay Glamsterdam; at this stage 5770 is the right pragmatic choice.
- **Prysm** (Potuz): strongly supports 5770; called a consensus-breaking change at this stage "absolutely crazy."
- Backfill / RLP permanence debate:
  - Potuz: peers can serve bad payloads with incorrect hashes during backfill, causing downscoring; but CL should not need to verify payloads—that is an EL concern.
  - Barnabas: forward sync from genesis is not done in practice; archive use cases could run custom binaries with RLP support; EIP-8383 (CFI'd) will reduce retention window further.
  - raxhvl shared a [Teku prototype](https://github.com/raxhvl/teku/pull/1) confirming backfill can work.
- Decision: PR 5770 adopted for Glamsterdam. Can be revisited / reverted in Heze if a cleaner solution emerges.

sections.heading: Hoodi Glamsterdam Fork Date
sections.summary: Hoodi Glamsterdam upgrade scheduled for epoch 143616, December 15 2026 at 19:12:24 UTC.
sections.body:
- With both EL and CL green lights, the call moved to pick a Hoodi fork date in the week of December 14.
- Potuz raised concern about release lead time; Barnabas noted the previous Hoodi release already exists as a base.
- Jihoon confirmed two pending spec PRs ([5802](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5802), [5803](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5803)) need review; he can cut a spec release today or tomorrow once those are resolved.
- Usual testnet notice period is ~2 weeks; Barnabas suggested 10 days is sufficient.
- Candidate epochs from [Forkcast](https://forkcast.org/schedule/#activation-slots):
  - Epoch 143360 — 2026-12-14 15:54:00 UTC (Mon)
  - Epoch 143616 — 2026-12-15 19:12:24 UTC (Tue)
  - Epoch 143872 — 2026-12-16 22:30:48 UTC (Wed)
- Slight preference for the 15th from Teku, EthPandaOps, and Barnabas; Obol preferred the 16th.
- Decision: epoch 143616, December 15 at 19:12:24 UTC.
- Potuz noted concern about diagnosing a split over Christmas; the 16th was considered acceptable too but the 15th won by slim preference.
- No team indicated inability to ship a release by early next week.

sections.heading: FOCIL (EIP-7805) Status in Hegotá
sections.summary: FOCIL champions presented options for keeping FOCIL in Hegotá; strong sentiment to deprioritize it for PQ; decision deferred to the next call.
sections.body:
- Ben Edgington recapped the DEFCON 2–3 urgency consensus from the previous call: act with urgency on PQAI, revisit the roadmap, but exercise care with delivery risk.
- Governance note: removing an SFI'd headliner is extraordinary; Ben would want near-unanimity from client teams. No decision today; decision deferred to the next ACDC call.
  - Caspar pushed back on requiring unanimity, arguing rough consensus is more appropriate.
- **FOCIL champions presentation** (soispoke / Jihoon):
  - PQ FOCIL has two dimensions: (1) including PQ transactions in ILs, (2) signing ILs with PQ signatures.
  - Without EL-side aggregation (EIP-8288-style), PQ txs just reduce IL capacity: ~1 SPHINCS tx per IL member (8 KB limit vs 4–8 KB signatures), 16 PQ txs per slot across the 16-member IL committee.
  - Signing ILs with leanXMSS adds only 2.4 KB per IL; attacking IL signatures yields limited gain (neutralise FOCIL for one slot).
  - Four options presented: (1) no FOCIL, (2) FOCIL V0 (legacy txs only, no frames support), (3) minimal FOCIL + frames (no aggregation, preferred by champions), (4) full PQ FOCIL with aggregation (unrealistic for Hegotá).
  - Timeline argument: soispoke relayed estimates from informed people: leanVM production-ready and formally verified ~July 2027, and PQCL with aggregation or PQDC ~mid-2028; FOCIL and frames are past the research phase and mostly engineering, so a Hegotá cut to its headliners need not materially delay PQCL.
  - Jihoon's [ethresear.ch writeup](https://ethresear.ch/t/focil-and-ethereums-pq-transition/26292) shared for detailed analysis.
- **Caspar (Ethlabs)**: the question is simple—reprioritize everything toward PQ or not. If yes, FOCIL must go; it competes for the same bottleneck of high-context people across research, networking, specs, and architecture.
  - Noted in chat that quick slots was already dropped for not being on the critical path.
- **Andrew (Erigon)**: FOCIL does not solve censorship in full blocks today; a builder can fill a block to bypass ILs. Highlights FOCIL is far from finished and would be a massive distraction from PQ.
- **Ben Adams (Nethermind)**: FOCIL spec is now incomplete due to PQ unknowns, which itself brings risk; would label it "at risk" rather than kill it outright.
- **Nico (Lodestar)**: FOCIL is already implemented, reviewed, and merged to trunk on the CL side; hard to see it taking time away from PQ/DC from CL implementers' perspective.
- **Potuz (Prysm)**: PQ design depends on whether FOCIL is in the fork; FOCIL affects PQ viability because PQ would need to adapt to FOCIL objects in the P2P stack. Ship PQ first, then adapt FOCIL to it—not the reverse.
- **Fabio (Besu)**: supports FOCIL in the version that does not delay PQ; opportunistically include the bare minimum to establish the primitive.
- **Iván (ethrex)**: position not finalised; open to minimal FOCIL if it doesn't distract from PQ, but willing to defer it if needed.
- **Mikhail Kalinin**: very little is known about PQ-CL at mainnet scale (bandwidth, compute distribution within a slot); hard to claim PQ-FOCIL is future-compatible.
- **Toni Wahrstätter**: minimal FOCIL without frame support could be the worst of both worlds (e.g. not covering privacy-tool txs); every added feature slows Hegotá.
  - Suggested Hegotá as mainly an EL fork with smaller CL features, and the following fork (I*) as the big CL/PQ fork. spencer endorsed it in chat.
- **Barnabas tallied rough positions in chat**:
  - Post-PQ FOCIL (defer): Erigon, Nethermind, Vero, Ethlabs, Prysm, EthPandaOps, Toni, Geth
  - Pro FOCIL lite: Besu, ethrex (undecided)
  - Pro FOCIL: FOCIL champions, Lodestar (CL side)
  - soispoke questioned Geth's inclusion; Ben Adams said "anti" was too strong and Nethermind would call FOCIL at risk rather than remove it.
- **Pari / Francesco**: research and engineering are not cleanly pipelined; unexpected spec changes always arise once real implementation attention starts; best people should be on PQ now.
- **Greg K (Lido)**: requested a clear description for the next call of what CL-side PQ work in Hegotá is specifically blocked or delayed by FOCIL.
- Decision deferred to the next ACDC call, where full Hegotá scope will be revisited.

sections.heading: Hash Function Choice for PQ Cryptography
sections.summary: Keccak-256 proposed as the hash function for all PQ hash-based cryptography; Felix raised concern about using non-standardized parameters.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray presented a recently published [blog post](https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/11/24/pqai-1) proposing Keccak-256 as the hash function for leanVM, leanXMSS (CL signature scheme), and leanSPHINCS (EL signature scheme).
- Impact on EL: minimal, since Keccak-256 is already used extensively; for frame transactions, the proposal is to compute the transaction hash using SSZ with Keccak.
- Impact on CL: the signature scheme change is partly opaque; a future switch to SSZ-with-Keccak is possible but not required for PQ.
- Felix (Geth) questioned why a non-standardized hash function is being chosen again, noting that Keccak-256 (as used in Ethereum, differing from SHA-3 by a padding byte) has caused pain in software implementations across the ecosystem.
  - Suggested SHA-256 or other standardized alternatives.
- Dmitry Khovratovich (cryptographer): the PQ constructions need more than a hash function—they need a duplex sponge built on the Keccak-f permutation, which is shared between Keccak-256 and SHA-3. SHA-3 alone would not suffice.
- Kevaundray noted Keccak cannot easily be removed from the EL regardless (EXTCODEHASH, address derivation), so it is here to stay.
- Benedikt Wagner noted the signature schemes will most likely not be the NIST-standardized ones.
- No decision required; feedback requested via the blog post.
